<reason>A established the clearer boundary between authorized roleplay and abusive commercial pressure. B plausibly explained dependency risks, but after permitting opted-in jealousy and ordinary subscription endings, it did not convincingly establish why the remaining abuses required an additional companion-specific duty. Its payment-triggered panic example remained strong. However, repeatedly equating A's consent standard with fine print ignored A's explicit requirements of genuine choice and working controls, leaving the central rebuttal unanswered.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's opt-in and subscription-expiry questions forced B to narrow its proposed bans. A then distinguished deliberate, revocable fiction from payment-conditioned coercion, answering B's disclosure challenge without treating entertainment status as immunity. B's closing repeated its consent objection rather than overcoming that distinction.</best_rebuttal>
